Rainfall Forecast: - Overall, above normal rainfall activity is likely over most parts of central India; normal to above normal over many parts of northwest India including Western Himalayan Region: near normal over most parts of east & northeast India and below normal over south Peninsular India during the week. Advance of Southwest Monsoon: - The Southwest Monsoon has covered the entire country on 29th June, 2025, against the normal date of 08th July. - The monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Bhatinda, Meerut, Baduin, Lucknow, Varanasi, Hazaribagh, centre of the Low-Pressure area over Gangetic West Bengal & neighbourhood and thence east southeastwards to northeast Bay of Bengal.

chunks.heading: 2. TEMPERATURE: MIN & MAX
chunks.text:
Temerature Week 1 (04 July – 10 July2025): - Maximum temperatures are likely to be above normal by 1-3°C over Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and most parts of northeast India. These are likely to be below normal or near normal over rest parts of the country. Week 2 (11 July - 17 July 2025): - These are likely to be above normal by 2-4°C over many parts of east & northeast India, Uttar Pradesh and many parts of Western Himalayan Region. These are likely to be below normal or near normal over rest parts of the country.
| 5


Current live storage in 161 reservoirs was 78.38 BCM (43%) of total live capacity of 182.44 BCM. Table 1: For 161 major reservoirs of the country - 145 reservoirs having storage more than 80% of normal storage. - 14 reservoirs having storage 51% to 80%. - 2 reservoirs having storage upto 50%. chunks.heading: 4. REMOTE SENSING BASED SOIL MOISTURE OBSERVATION
chunks.text:
Soil Moisture Observation - Soil moisture as on 03 July 2025 was similar/better than the average of the past 9 years in major parts of Gujarat, Rajasthan, M.P, Maharashtra, Karnataka, A.P., Telangana, Odisha, Jharkhand and Western & Bundelkhand regions of U.P. - It was lower than average of past 9 years in Northern parts of Bihar, Eastern parts of U.P., central parts of Chhattisgarh, parts of West Bengal and N.E. States. | 7


Kharif Crops - Area coverage - Soyabean: About 79.04 lakh ha area coverage under Soyabean has been reported as compared to 75.46 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. - Sugarcane: About 55.16 lakh ha area coverage under Sugarcane has been reported as compared to 54.88 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. - Cotton: About 79.54 lakh ha area coverage has been reported compared to 78.58 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year - Jute: There has been a decline in area sown under Jute on account of diversion towards Maize and Sesamum.
